Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question, and you will be prompted to provide your name and company. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's third quarter results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, our Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our powerhouse brands in snacks like NutriCrunch and NutriBites, beverages such as ThirstQuench and Sparkle Hydrate, and personal care lines including GlowEssence and FreshGlow. We're navigating a dynamic environment marked by moderating inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and supply chain normalization, while staying laser-focused on executing our strategic priorities of premiumization, operational efficiency, and data-driven marketing.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects central to our performance: first, our pricing actions and their impact on sales; second, the effectiveness of our marketing campaigns; third, our A&P spending and return on investment; and fourth, our gross margin guidance and key assumptions underpinning it.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan Patel to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Patel:  
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter across the board. Net sales were $7.2 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year, with organic growth of 4.8% driven by robust pricing realization and mix benefits. Gross margin expanded to 48.5%, up 130 basis points year-over-year, propelled by sustained pricing discipline, moderating input costs, and supply chain productivity gains. Operating income reached $1.1 billion, reflecting effective cost management, while diluted earnings per share came in at $1.25. We continue to manage our costs effectively while investing aggressively in long-term growth initiatives like our high-margin innovations and omnichannel expansion.

Let me dive deeper into these results, starting with our pricing actions and their impact on sales performance, which formed a cornerstone of our 5.2% net revenue growth this quarter. In an environment where global CPI inflation eased to around 3.1% but key commodities like cocoa, palm oil, and PET resin for our packaging stayed elevated—up 12-15% year-over-year—we executed disciplined, data-driven pricing strategies across our approximately $28 billion portfolio. This mix of list price hikes, promotional resets, and trade spend optimization contributed a solid +7.1% to our net revenue growth, more than offsetting a -1.9% volume headwind and supported by +3.0% from favorable product mix.

On list pricing, we rolled out targeted increases averaging 6.8%, ranging from 4% on high-velocity staples like ValueFresh laundry detergents—where we defended share against private label pushes from Walmart's Great Value or Aldi's expansions—to 11-12% in premium areas such as Indulge chocolate confections and GlowBeauty skincare. These were phased in starting earlier in the year, with 70% of SKUs adjusted by quarter-end. In North America, our biggest market at 45% of sales, we averaged +8.2%, stabilizing everyday retail pricing amid tariff risks and a 4% uptick in ocean freight.

Elasticity came in stronger than expected—actuals at -2.1x versus our pre-action SymphonyIRI and Nielsen forecasts of -3.5x—bolstered by brand strength and premiumization. Take our CraveRight bar line in snacks: a 9% list price rise drove +5.2% average selling price growth with just -1.4% volume drop, netting +6.8% category growth, much like Mondelez's cocoa pass-through success. Regionally, EMEA at 25% of sales saw +5.4% pricing amid EU inflation at 2.8% and softening sentiment like Germany's GfK index down 7% year-over-year; we shifted to high-low promos, trimming trade spend to 15% of gross revenue via AI event calendars with Tesco and Carrefour, yielding +4.1% NRG from pricing and flat volumes as shoppers traded up to Resist plant-based yogurt packs, gaining 120 basis points in ACV distribution.

In emerging markets—20% of sales—we hit +10.3%, navigating LATAM currency weakness like Brazil's real down 8% and India's 5.9% inflation. Brazil's Frescura beverages absorbed 14% hikes tied to 22% sugar inflation, holding volumes to -0.8% via sachet packs and informal trade, boosting market share 210 basis points per Kantar. APAC got +9.1%, countering Alibaba and Flipkart discounts with dynamic pricing via our Oracle revenue system scraping competitor ERPs and modeling elasticities.

We've enhanced this with our Pricing Excellence Center of Excellence, where 25 data scientists use a Google Cloud Vertex AI engine simulating 10,000 scenarios per SKU weekly, factoring USDA forecasts and Bloomberg futures—it optimized pass-through like 85% of 16% cocoa inflation into chocolate lines, slashing decision times from eight weeks to three days. We also refined promos: 20% shallower buy-one-get-one depth in North America, more frequency on hero SKUs, preserving gross margins at 32.4% up 110 basis points and curbing cannibalization.

Overall, organic NRG reached +7.3%, with pricing and mix dominating; our top 20 power brands at 55% of sales grew +9.2% as consumers premiumized, like shifting to EcoShield pods up 15%. We saw pressure in mass household care volumes down 4.2% from dollar store privates, offset by +12% e-comm growth where willingness-to-pay runs 8-10% higher per IRI. This aligns with our Value Discipline Framework for the trade-down yet aspirational consumer. Looking ahead, with commodities like cocoa futures down 8% post-harvest, we'll hold lists steady but flex promos dynamically, tracking elasticity via our consumer health index blending Nielsen panels and Brandwatch social listening above 70% value perception. Pilots for retailer revenue-sharing in Europe, like P&G's Costco model, are underway.

Shifting to the effectiveness of our marketing campaigns, our disciplined, data-driven approach delivered a robust 12% year-over-year increase in marketing ROI, hitting 4.7x overall—beating our 4.0x internal target and the 3.5x CPG benchmark from Kantar's latest Media Reactions report. This is the third straight quarter of improvement, highlighting our precision marketing pivot amid softening sentiment and A&P inflation.

Total A&P was $485 million, up 8% year-over-year but flat sequentially thanks to zero-based budgeting, ditching low-ROI legacy TV for digital and retail media networks now at 65% of mix versus 25% traditional. Our Vital Refresh summer push on beverages—extending Sparkle Hydrate like PepsiCo's Gatorade Win from Within—spent $120 million for 6.2x ROAS, 22% IRI sales lift, and 4.2-point household penetration gain to 28% among urban millennials 18-34. Geo-holdouts confirmed 14% causal uplift above our 10% scale threshold; CAC fell 15% to $12.50 per new household, CLV/CAC at 3.8x with 18% repeat growth via loyalty apps. Multi-touch attribution using Google's Meridian and our CDP shifted 30% credit to CTV awareness, stabilizing CPMs at $18 below industry $25+.

In snacks, Crunch Time for NutriBites—echoing Unilever's Ben & Jerry's sustainability plays with 75% recycled packaging—spent $65 million for 5.1x ROAS, 9% Nielsen share gain via 50 micro-influencers at 50k followers with 8% engagement and 3.2% converting shoppable TikTok Lives.

Regionally: North America (55% spend) at 5.3x ROAS, Walmart Connect and Amazon DSP driving 25% incremental volume and 12% basket share plus 3-point ACV to 92% against Aldi pressure. Europe (20%) at 3.9x amid 7% inflation versus wages, above Reckitt peers; 40% more to in-store screens at Tesco/Carrefour lifted impulse 11% for GlowEssence like L'Oréal efficacy ads. APAC (15%) stellar 6.8x, China Tmall Double 11 KOLs up 32% e-comm for Sparkle, India JioMart vernacular WhatsApp rural +16%. LATAM (10%) 4.2x, Brazil Mercado Libre RMN at 7x despite Mexico forex.

Forward, our Marketing Science team launched AI dynamic creative optimization via The Trade Desk—1,200 variants per campaign for 28% video completion uplift—and $15 million LiveRamp clean room for privacy-safe matching post-cookies. Agile pods like P&G's model run 6-week sprints with real-time MMM, cutting waste 22% to health & wellness now 35% of portfolio versus indulgence softening 5% per Circana. Q4 A&P up 5-7% targeting 5.0x+ ROAS scaling Vitality Club DTC at 2.5 million members, 45% retention, monitoring tariffs.

Next, on A&P spend and ROI overall—wrapping up a resilient year navigating inflation and bifurcated demand—FY 2024 to date mirrors our full-year trajectory with $2.58 billion deployed at 12.8% of net sales, up 80 basis points from prior, above our 11-13% target on brand equity conviction. Q3 alone $680 million at 13.1%, holiday-heavy for SnackAttack and PureThirst.

ROMI averaged 3.6x via proprietary MMM validated by Nielsen/Kantar, up 15% from 3.1x prior, generating $9.3 billion incremental revenue with 9-month payback—high-end versus P&G/Unilever 3-4x. Channel shift: digital/shopper at 42% up from 28%, TV 35% with 18% linear cuts to CTV/TikTok/YouTube; SnackAttack Crave the Crunch at 5.2x for Gen Z. In-store/trade 23% at 2.8x via AI planograms at Walmart/Kroger.

By category, Household & Personal Care at 14.2% of sales, 4.1x ROMI, 2.1-point ACV gain for FreshGlow/GlowEssence. Food & Beverage $450 million at 3.2x, RMNs/Amazon DSP 60% efficiency. North America (55% spend, $1.42 billion) 3.9x with Target Circle/Instacart +22% penetration. EMEA (25%, $645 million) 3.4x, UK/Germany sustainability promos for PureThirst recycled packs aligning EU Green Deal. APAC (15%, $387 million) 3.1x despite China echoes, WeChat Mini-Programs 7x e-comm Southeast Asia, India Blinkit +150 bps salty snacks. LATAM (5%, $129 million) 2.9x, Brazil geo-fenced mobile.

Key enablers: AI DMP with The Trade Desk/CRM from 45 million loyalty members cut waste 24%, +0.4x ROMI; causal AI MMM with BlackCurve incorporating CPI/confidence reallocated $150 million from TV to CTV amid strikes; zero-based planning via GCB Rewards app at 28 million users, 85%+ accuracy.

For FY2024 end, A&P at 12.5-13.0% of sales, digital to 50%, creator economy like FreshGlow Instagram Reels, connected retail AR pilots with Albertsons/Carrefour projecting 4.5x amid IRI +1.5% CPG growth.

Finally, our gross margin outlook remains a profitability cornerstone. Q3 adjusted gross margin hit 48.5%, +130 basis points year-over-year and +50 sequentially—third straight expansion quarter, trailing four-quarter average 47.8% above 46-47% floor, outpacing peers like Mondelez on cocoa.

We're raising full-year FY2024 guidance to 49.0-50.0% from 48.0-49.0%, implying 120-200 basis points expansion; Q4 at 49.8-50.3% assuming no FX shocks—sustainable via trifecta: inputs +150 bps, pricing +80 bps, volume/mix +30 bps, supply chain +60 bps.

Inputs (55% COGS): cocoa down 12% QoQ/flat YoY post-West Africa/El Niño peaks, palm -8% YoY Indonesia normalization, dairy stable post-Ukraine; FY flat to -2-3% with 85% hedges, conservative on EMEA energy +5%. Diversified basket (15% cocoa vs. Hershey 30%+) edges Kellogg/Hershey.

Pricing: H1 7.2% realized, NGPR +6.5% post-trade; 9-11% lists on NutriCrunch/ThirstQuench Zero (25% YoY growth, 12% mix), offset promos; elasticity -2.5 to -3.0 better than -3.5 Nielsen. H2 4-5% for 3-4% NGPR, optimizing AUR vs. private label +15% IRI NA share.

Volume/mix: Q3 +2.1% volume led e-comm/convenience +5%, mix +1.8 points; exited low-margin legacies +40 bps, RTD/clean snacks 28% sales up from 22%. Guide 1-2% volume, 1.5-point mix from non-alc RTD 12% CAGR Euromonitor; AI demand sensing 92% accuracy.

Supply chain CPG NextGen: 2.1% Q3 COGS savings—Ohio robotics +18% throughput/-0.8 labor point, Mexico rollouts; Perfect Day fermentation -15% pilots to 10% volume FY25, RSPO palm; freight -20% YoY, Vietnam nearshoring -5% APAC, turns 6.2x from 5.4x. 1.5-2.0% flow-through to 300 bps 3-year target.

Regions: NA (60% sales) 51.2% Q3, guide 51-52%; EMEA (20%) 45.8% to 46-47%; APAC/LATAM (20%) 47.5%, volume offsets 3% BRL FX.

Risks: 1% input adverse =30 bps hit, 10% USD strength -20 bps; upside mix/savings. FY2025 50%+ trajectory like General Mills/Colgate vigilance but ahead.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for questions: please press star one, then your name and company. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan.

Mike Johnson:  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Alex Rivera:  
Thanks, Mike. Inflation's moderation has been a tailwind, but we've seen bifurcated behavior—traders down in staples but holding premium in health and indulgence. Our pricing elasticity at -2.1x reflects sticky brand loyalty, with premium innovations like ThirstQuench Zero up 25% despite hikes. Shopper marketing and loyalty data show resilience above 70% value perception, even as GfK indices soften in EMEA. We're balancing affordability with tiers to capture aspirational spend.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Lisa Chen:  
Regarding your new product Sparkle Hydrate Zero, what are the projections for its market impact?

Mia Chen:  
Hi Lisa, great question. Sparkle Hydrate Zero, our plant-based RTD extension, is projecting 15-20% category share capture in non-alc hydration within 12 months, building on Vital Refresh's 6.2x ROAS and 22% sales lift. Early tests show 32% e-comm growth in APAC via KOLs, 16% rural India penetration, and 4.2-point millennial household gains. With clinical efficacy claims and DTC Vitality Club scaling to 2.5 million members at 45% retention, we see it driving 1.5-point overall mix shift, targeting 12% CAGR per Euromonitor.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:  
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Jordan Patel:  
Sure, David. Promos were optimized within our $680 million Q3 A&P at 13.1% of sales, focusing high-ROI shopper tactics—23% of mix at 2.8x ROMI via AI planograms in Walmart/Kroger. We cut BOGO depth 20% in NA, boosted frequency on heroes, reducing trade from 18% to 15% gross in EMEA. This preserved NGPR +6.5%, minimized cannibalization, and contributed to 3.6x overall ROMI with $9.3 billion incremental revenue. FY guide 12.5-13.0% keeps intensity high for 2-3% volume amid peers' softening.

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We're confident in our ability to navigate the current environment—leveraging pricing discipline, marketing precision, A&P efficiency, and margin levers—to deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
